reply.summary: Your foundation fits Argus because it is built for the same person and the same moment: someone on their own server, often at night, reading plain-language explanations of what broke. Dark surfaces, calm rounded headings and tall clear body text keep long reading comfortable, and the cool greys stay out of the way while #28a4f0, #14b8a6 and #a855f7 mark the important parts. Everything sends people cleanly to the GitHub repo and the docs without decoration getting in the way.
reply.rule: #28a4f0 is the brand colour and carries the main actions and links, like the GitHub and docs buttons, while #14b8a6 and #a855f7 appear only as small supporting highlights and the grey neutrals hold all the ordinary surfaces and text.

reasons.surface: Dark matches how Argus is used: people watch metrics and containers for long stretches and often at night when something breaks, so easier-on-the-eyes dark backgrounds mean less strain.
reasons.display-type: Sora's round, geometric letters read as modern and calm on a dark background, which keeps headings about the AI investigator and the likely root cause pleasant to scan.
reasons.body-type: Source Sans 3 is open-source like Argus, and its tall lowercase letters keep log lines, metric labels and root-cause paragraphs clear at 14px on dark while staying quiet under Sora.
reasons.type-scale: 16px body with headings at ×1.25 is comfortable for long plain-language root cause text and the docs, yet still fits metrics and container lists on one screen in dark mode.
reasons.brand-color: #28a4f0 is a bright, clear blue that stands out on the dark surface, so the GitHub and docs calls to action are obvious at a glance.
reasons.secondary-color: #14b8a6 gives a second supporting highlight that reads as calm and technical, useful for secondary emphasis without competing with the brand colour.
reasons.accent-color: #a855f7 adds a distinct accent for small moments like the AI investigator, so it feels separate and special without taking over.
reasons.neutral: Cool greys sit naturally beside the blue brand colour and keep large dark areas, panels and text quiet so the data itself stands out.
reasons.semantics: #16a34a, #d97706 and #dc2626 give green for healthy, amber for warning and red for error, which is exactly the language a monitoring tool needs when something goes wrong.
reasons.spacing: A tight 4px base keeps metrics, container lists and log lines dense and scannable, which suits a tool that shows a lot of numbers on one screen.
reasons.radius: Soft 8px corners take the hard edge off panels and buttons, so a dense dark dashboard still feels calm rather than sharp.
reasons.depth: Subtle shadows give just enough separation between panels and popups on the dark background, without heavy effects that would fight the data.
